messages:
maria-chen: Heads up — ran microbenchmarks on torch.compile + CUDA graph capture for hot path tuning. Observed surprise kernel choice on matmul at seqlen=256 where the autotuner picked a workspace-heavy kernel; that path shows ~1.7x latency vs eager.

ajay-singh: huh. do you have the traces / nvprof / nsight output?

maria-chen: pasting the condensed perf snippet from nvprof (kernel names from runtime logs):
```text
seqlen=128: kernel=matmul_fp16_small_workspace    time=9.2ms
seqlen=256: kernel=matmul_fp16_large_workspace    time=17.5ms  <-- regression
seqlen=512: kernel=matmul_fp16_small_workspace    time=15.4ms
```

maria-chen: note: when torch.compile is OFF, autotuner consistently picks small_workspace and times are ~10-11ms for seqlen=256. So this smells like an interaction with compile/capture.

jamie-ross: interesting — cudagraph capture + torch.compile might be freezing a kernel choice based on shapes seen during capture. capture-time shapes could bias the tuner.

luis: also consider KV cache state during capture. If warmup populates KV cache, the effective matmul dims can be different. Did you capture with primed cache? @maria-chen

maria-chen: yes — capture was done during warmup with KV cache primed for a 512-prefix. I suspected KV offsets could make the traced matmul look like a different shape.

perf-bot: detected anomaly: perf_regression detected on ci/torchcompile-hotpath (latency +73% at seqlen=256)

ajay-singh: steps to reproduce? script / branch?

maria-chen: repro steps: branch runtime/torchcompile-kernel-probe, script ./bench/run_capture.sh --model gpt-small --seqlen 256 --warmup 100 --use_cudagraph --log-kernel-select

jamie-ross: quick test: re-run capture with KV cache empty, and also with torch.compile=off. If kernel choice flips back, we can attribute to capture-time shapes/cache.

maria-chen: running both variants now, will collect kernel_select logs and nvtx ranges. sharing results in ~20-30m.

luis: if confirmed, mitigation options: 1) normalize KV offsets during capture (zero-out cache), 2) mark dims dynamic for capture, or 3) force re-run autotune post-capture. Also check architecture-aware scoring (sm75 vs sm80 heuristics).

ajay-singh: also add env RUNTIME_LOG=kernel_select to get verbose decision traces during the run. and capture the autotuner candidates / scores.

maria-chen: added that. one more thing: our batching heuristic probe can merge in-flight sequences during capture probing, skewing the seqlen distribution. I'll include batch hist with the run.

jamie-ross: if reproducible, we need a perf regression test in the harness and a guard in the cudagraph capture path so capture doesn't permanently bias kernel selection.

maria-chen: follow-up results: re-ran with empty KV cache at capture time => kernel=matmul_fp16_small_workspace, time=10.8ms. capture with primed cache => large_workspace 17.5ms. so it's cache-dependent and reproducible.

ajay-singh: ok actionable list: A) normalize/clear KV cache during capture; B) when torch.compile+CUDAgraph used, force dynamic dim path or re-run autotune post-capture; C) add a runtime warning when capture sees cache != empty.

maria-chen: filed issue runtime#8423 with logs and perf traces, assigning eng-runtime + eng-ml for design review.

jamie-ross: :thumbsup:

perf-bot: created issue runtime#8423

maria-chen: will send a short PR to add a capture-time normalization flag and a unit in the perf harness to catch this regression. thanks all for the quick triage.
